questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses offered, language and culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation session with all the information we needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation session, contact with the International Office

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Oead - apply early

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think TU Wien has housing for students on campus. Nonetheless, if possible, I recommend living close to the city centre

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I needed to attend the orientation session in person in September in order to receive my credentials and register to courses. Courses only start in October, but if I didn't do the registration in early September I might not have been able to secure a spot in all the courses I was interested in

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office at TU Wien was quick to answer questions and provide us with all the information we needed

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the classes I initially selected when applying for the exchange were not offered this semester, but I was able to register to some new courses offered for the first time

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try completing the registration as early as possible. The date of the orientation session you attended can be considered the first day of your exchange, so if you want you can go earlier and have some time to visit the city, you won't have too much time when you start the courses if you're going for 30 ECTS

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took were either 3 ECTS or 6 ECTS. The 3 ECTS ones are not that difficult and the workload is relatively low, but the 6 ECTS ones can be quite demanding. All the information about the courses, including examination modalities and workload is explained on the website and some courses have a longer registration period so that you can attend the first class and decide if it's for you

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I feel like the professors can be a lot more involved with the students directly for help and feedback with homework, not just the TAs. There were also a lot of guest lectures as part of most courses from professors from other universities or industry experts, which I appreciated.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AI Ethics, Sustainability in Computer Science, Foundations of Ubiquitous Computing and IoT, Design Thinking: Ideation, Generative AI, Intelligent User Interfaces, Technology Work and Organization

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AI Ethics was a really interesting course, offered for the first time this semester and will be offered every semester from now on (winter and summer semester). Also Foundations of Ubiquitous Computing and IoT is fun if you like building things yourself

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was charged a cleaning fee after I left of 750 dkk, not because I left the room dirty (that would result in your deposit not being returned completely), but because this was the rule at my housing. Originally this was supposed to be 375dkk, but they increased it when I moved in in October

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected but ordering is more affordable than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can join a sports class through USI. I joined two classes per week and paid a total of 750dkk for the entire semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN has a lot of activities and trips planned. I didn't participate in a lot of them since I was also working and my schedule was full, but they are quite cheap and I only heard positive things from the people that participated. Also the USI classes are cheap if you want to do sports while on your exchange

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot to see in Vienna and around Vienna. I recommend hiking trips when the weather is good and museums otherwise. Most museums offer student discounts. Also sometimes there are free events at museums, so keep an eye on social media for that. Also I recommend going to concerts and to the opera

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is not hard, but speaking German helps

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think cultural differences are that big

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and overall the culture of the city - it is full of art, music and history

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Choose courses carefully, there are a lot of very good options
Get involved in other activities too - ESN Buddynetwork is very active here
Learn a little bit of German

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: These questions are very similar, I don't know what else to say

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really liked most of the courses I took, they are generally very well organized and very up-to-date with the existing research in the field

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing 30 ECTS at TU Wien while also working is definitely challenging. Most students here go for lower than 30 ECTS per semester and choose to graduate later. I recommend choosing the courses carefully, based on your interests and the required workload

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
